newsitem.title: SWEDEN: FORECAST-Sweden's repo rate seen unchanged on Tue.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Sweden's repo rate seen unchanged on Tue.

text.p: Sweden's central bank, the Riksbank, is expected to keep its key repurchase rate, the repo, unchanged at 4.10 percent on Tuesday, according to a Reuter poll of 12 economists.

The economists point to the crown's volatility and softness as well as Riksbank governor Urban Backstrom's speech last week, in which he said monetary policy was well measured and that time was needed to evalute effects of previous cuts.
The Riksbank has not cut the repo rate this year, but in 1996 it lowered it to 4.10 percent from 8.91 percent.
"Backstrom's speech indicates that there will not be a cut right now," said Sven-Arne Svensson, economist at Hagstromer & Qviberg.
"But (among fundamentals) there really is only the crown speaking against a cut and the crown will probably strengthen."
High unemployment, low inflation expectations and improved state finances make continued cuts possible, he said.
While seven of the economists forecast further cuts in the future, four thought the repo had hit bottom at the current level and one did not have a view.
"There will at least be one more cut of 20 basis points," said Bjorn Englund, economist at Danish banking group Unibank.
"But I think the Riksbank will hold off for a while, at least until its inflation report on March 20 and probably longer."
Those doubting future cuts are pointing to an upturn in economic trends.
"A recovery in the industrial sector seems to be on its way and no further monetary stimulation is probably needed," said Dick Woodworth, economist at Merrill Lynch.
